reason: Cohen & Steers is an active investment manager of real assets and alternative income. It earns fees on assets under management from its own funds and separate accounts. Morningstar's website presents it as an investment research company offering fund, ETF and stock analysis, ratings, data and portfolio tools. Its revenue is mainly subscriptions, data and index licensing, and ratings fees. Morningstar does have a small managed-portfolio line, and both firms deal with advisors and institutions. But Morningstar mostly sells information and software to investors and asset managers, and Cohen & Steers mostly sells managed investment products.
reason_if_0: Different business model. Morningstar earns most of its money from research, data and software subscriptions, licensing and ratings fees. Cohen & Steers earns AUM-based management fees on its own real-asset and alternative-income strategies. Morningstar's asset managers are customers of its research, not rivals in what it sells.
